Mechanical screening of the 45-condition RAP matrix (Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl with nine heat treatments) includes this 500 °C/24 h, 2 wt.% Al sample; tensile testing at room temperature with initial strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹.

Hot rolling and water quenching resulted in a fully recrystallized microstructure with a grain size of ~20 μm; this is the only grain-size value reported for the RAP Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl materials (refers to the hot-rolled/water-quenched state).
The Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al composition (Al < 5 wt.%) is single-phase austenite at room temperature; austenite is the fcc phase of the Fe-Mn-Al-C system.
Microstructure of the 2 wt.% Al sample: single austenite phase (Al < 5 wt.%) with recrystallized ~20 μm grain size and retained Mn microsegregations.
The paper states that for Al content below 5 wt.% (this sample is 2 wt.% Al), a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature.

overall_structure.value: Single-phase austenitic (fcc) microstructure at room temperature; fully recrystallized after hot rolling and water quenching, with some retained Mn microsegregations.

source.reason: Structure record for this Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al sample aged 500 °C/24 h, based on the single-austenite phase field (Al < 5 wt.%) and the recrystallized grain size after hot rolling and water quenching.

unmapped_findings: This sample belongs to the intermediate Al range (2–6 wt.% Al); the paper states these intermediate alloys have mechanical properties between those of Fe-30Mn-1.2C (which weakens/embrittles on aging) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (which strengthens on aging), and that aging has a much smaller influence on their tensile behavior.

Specific numeric YS/UTS/TE values for the 500 °C/24 h condition at 2 wt.% Al are only shown graphically in Fig. 3 (and selected results in Fig. 4); they are not numerically reported in the text. Fig. 3a indicates YS ≈ 350–450 MPa across 0–4 wt.% Al, Fig. 3b indicates UTS reaches a minimum near 2 wt.% Al, Fig. 3c indicates TE drops to a minimum at 2 wt.% Al, and Fig. 3d indicates hardness ≈ 200 HBW across 0–6 wt.% Al.
As-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling and water quenching produced a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 μm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.

For Al contents below 5 wt.%, a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature and mechanical twinning (TWIP effect) is the dominant deformation mechanism, so this 2 wt.% Al sample is a single-phase austenitic TWIP (SIMPLEX) steel.

κ-carbides (L′1₂ structure, approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)₃AlC) can form on aging in Fe-Mn-Al-C steels, but the paper states the 2–6 wt.% Al intermediate variants do not show equivalent (κ-carbide) strengthening to the ~8 wt.% Al variant, implying negligible κ-carbide strengthening for this 2Al sample.
